report.summary: Chunk 3 of gated_writes.py: implements _PinnedWorktreeGit, _reattempt, _as_cancel_predicate, _CumulativeGateCancelled, and _promote_one_inner with staleness handling and cumulative gate logic.
risks: _promote_one_inner | medium | Uses _retried flag to limit regeneration attempts; if base keeps moving, the candidate is dropped. | Check if a loop could cause infinite recursion without the _retried guard.

_promote_one_inner | medium | Runs full test_command in cumulative gate; if test_command is long, cancellation may not be immediate. | Verify that _as_cancel_predicate(cancel) is called frequently enough.
_promote_one_inner | low | Raises _CumulativeGateCancelled on cancellation; caught by generic except. | Confirm that the caller handles this exception correctly.

_hardened_env | low | Some environment variables are popped; if they are not set, pop raises KeyError? pop with default avoids that. | Check that all popped keys are present in env or default is provided.
todos: Verify that _CumulativeGateCancelled is properly caught and handled in the caller.
Check that the _retried flag is correctly passed in recursion in _promote_one_inner.
Ensure that _as_cancel_predicate handles all expected cancel types correctly.

handoff.purpose: Implements git environment hardening, pinned worktree git calls, candidate reattempt, cancel predicate normalization, cumulative gate cancellation exception, and promotion inner logic.

claims.text: Every git call against ONE worktree, pinned to the admin dir read BEFORE any candidate-authored patch is applied into it.
claims.why: The class captures admin_dir at construction; run() uses it explicitly.

claims.text: Mirrors ``daedalus.spine.attempt``'s ``_read_gitdir_pointer`` + ``_git(..., git_dir=, work_tree=)`` pattern (independently written here; both are module-private there).
claims.why: The referenced pattern in another module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: a linked worktree's ``.git`` is a FILE containing ``gitdir: <path>``.
claims.why: _read_gitdir_pointer reads .git as text and checks for 'gitdir:' prefix.

claims.text: Once candidate-authored bytes have landed via ``git apply`` (see ``promote_candidates``), a later git call that re-resolves that pointer from disk is trusting a file the applied patch could have rewritten (measured, in ``attempt.py``'s own history, to let a candidate-authored ``.gitattributes`` spawn an arbitrary program via a config-bound filter/textconv driver).
claims.why: This refers to behavior in another module and historical incidents not in this chunk.

claims.text: So the pointer is read ONCE, at construction -- callers must construct this immediately after ``create_worktree`` and before the first ``git apply`` -- and every subsequent call is pinned to that captured path explicitly, never re-resolved from the (by-then possibly candidate-controlled) working tree.
claims.why: __init__ reads admin_dir; run() uses self.admin_dir and never re-reads .git.

claims.text: Re-run the SAME instruction/target_paths against a NEW base commit.
claims.why: The function creates a fresh spec with new base_revision and calls run_attempt.

claims.text: Used only when the integration branch has moved past the base a candidate's artifact was built against -- see ``promote_candidates``.
claims.why: The function promote_candidates is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A fresh ``TaskSpec`` (same content, new ``base_revision``) through the same ``TaskAttempt``/``offload_runner`` path as Phase 1: no new isolation mechanism, just the existing one invoked again with an updated base.
claims.why: The referenced TaskAttempt and offload_runner are not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``cancel`` is forwarded unchanged to this regeneration's own ``TaskAttempt`` -- see ``gate_candidates``' docstring for what it accepts.
claims.why: gate_candidates is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Normalise a cancel token to a zero-arg predicate, for the ONE call site in this module (the cumulative re-gate's ``RunnerContext.is_cancelled``, see ``_promote_one_inner``) that builds a ``RunnerContext`` directly rather than going through ``TaskAttempt`` (which does this normalisation itself, internally, for every ``cancel`` this module forwards via ``run_attempt``).
claims.why: _promote_one_inner does call _as_cancel_predicate(cancel) and passes it to RunnerContext.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT an import of ``daedalus.spine.attempt._as_predicate`` -- that name is module-private there, and this file's own convention is to mirror a small private helper rather than reach across another module's underscore boundary (see ``_read_gitdir_pointer`` above, which does the same for the same reason).
claims.why: The referenced function in another module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Same three-way contract as the original: ``None`` -> never cancelled; a callable -> called, a broken callable treated as "not cancelled" (a token that raises must not be able to abort work it was only supposed to observe); anything exposing ``is_set()`` (a ``threading.Event``, a ``KillSwitch``) -> that, same broken-token rule.
claims.why: The function implements exactly that: None->lambda: False, callable->try/except returning False on exception, else getattr is_set.

claims.text: The cumulative re-gate stopped because ``cancel`` fired, not because a test genuinely failed. Raised (never silently swallowed) so the SAME fabricated-verdict shape this repo already fixed once -- a cooperative stop reported as an ordinary gate failure -- cannot recur here: the ``except`` block below still resets the integration worktree exactly as it does for a real failure (that reset is unconditional and was already safe for cancellation before this class existed -- see the comment on that reset), but the REASON string a caller sees now says ``cancelled``, not ``gate failed``, so a loop driver reading ``reason`` back cannot mistake "I was asked to stop" for "this candidate is bad."
claims.why: The exception is raised in _promote_one_inner when gate_result.cancelled is True, and it is a distinct type from RuntimeError. The except block in _promote_one_inner (end of chunk) catches Exception, so it will be caught and presumably reset the worktree.

claims.text: STALENESS. Every candidate after the first, in the normal case of 2+ writes gated concurrently against one shared starting commit, WILL have artifact.base_revision != current_head the moment it is this candidate's turn -- that inequality is not an edge case here, it is the expected shape. A `git apply --check` passing would only prove the bytes still match; it says nothing about whether the change is still semantically correct now that an earlier candidate has landed ahead of it. So: regenerate against the current integration state instead of trusting a check. Bounded to ONE retry -- a second staleness hit means something is landing candidates faster than this one can be recomputed, which is a reason to stop and report, not to loop.
claims.why: The code checks artifact.base_revision != current_head, and if _retried is True, returns a failure reason. Otherwise calls _reattempt and recursively calls itself with _retried=True.

claims.text: NOTHING WRITTEN. `git apply` (no --3way, no --reject) validates the whole patch before writing anything; a non-zero exit here means the integration worktree is exactly as it was before this call. Refused and reported, never retried with a fuzzier match and never merged with conflict markers.
claims.why: The code returns immediately on non-zero returncode, without modifying the worktree further.

claims.text: WAS `lambda: False` (uncancellable) -- this is the one gate in the promote path that runs the project's WHOLE test command, so it is the longest-running thing a stop request can land inside. Safe to make cancellable: the `except` block just below already resets the integration worktree to `current_head` unconditionally on ANY failure here, cancellation included, so honouring `cancel` adds no new way to leave that worktree in a worse state than finishing would -- it only shortens how long a stop takes to land.
claims.why: The code now passes _as_cancel_predicate(cancel) as is_cancelled, making it cancellable. The comment explains the safety reasoning.

claims.text: Distinct exception type on purpose -- see _CumulativeGateCancelled's own docstring: the reason string a caller reads back must say "cancelled", never "gate failed", or this reintroduces the exact fabricated-verdict shape this parameter exists to close.
claims.why: The code raises _CumulativeGateCancelled with a message containing 'cancelled'.

observations.what: _promote_one_inner uses _retried flag to limit regeneration attempts; if base keeps moving, the candidate is dropped.
The cumulative gate test command runs with a timeout; cancellation is supported via _as_cancel_predicate.
_CumulativeGateCancelled is caught by the generic except Exception; the worktree reset is unconditional.
_as_cancel_predicate handles None, callable, and objects with is_set method.
_hardened_env removes several environment variables that could leak sensitive info or cause side effects.
